says.detail:
This page does not describe a compensation scheme, who decides compensation, any cap or threshold, free legal advice, or whether it stops a patient going to court. It only explains how to make a complaint to the Health Board, with an informal approach first and then a formal complaint if needed. For timing, it says a complaint should be made as quickly as possible, and if there is a good reason it may still be investigated as long as no more than a year has passed; acknowledgements are within two working days and a written response is aimed for within 30 working days, with investigations taking up to 6 months or longer in exceptional circumstances.
Quotes: "If you are unhappy with the treatment or care you are receiving, we would encourage you to raise your complaint as soon as possible" | "If there is a good reason why the complaint cannot be made sooner, it may still be possible to investigate your concerns, as long as no more than a year has passed." | "You will receive an acknowledgement letter within two working days of receipt of your formal complaint." | "The aim is for you to receive a written response to your complaint within 30 working days."

filled.value: Hello, I am Elin Rhydderch, and I am writing to ask about a possible medical negligence matter. On 12th September 2026, I slipped on wet steps and fell on my outstretched right hand. I went to the Emergency Unit at University Hospital of Wales, Heath Park, Cardiff, where an X-ray was done, and they said it was a sprain. I was sent home with a bandage and no follow-up. The pain did not go away. On 19th October 2026, my GP sent me for a repeat X-ray and MRI, which showed a displaced scaphoid waist fracture that has not healed. I now need surgery. I have missed class tests and weeks of shifts at my café job. I would like an explanation, an apology, changes to how A&E checks wrist injuries, and compensation for pain and lost earnings. I would also like to know how a case like this could be funded. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guideline D62 says: 'Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination.' Did the clinical examination at A&E sufficiently rule out a scaphoid fracture, and was MRI considered as first-line imaging as recommended? Please let me know if you can advise. You can reach me by email at elin.rhydderch@example.com or by phone on 07700 900582.

I went to the Emergency Unit at University Hospital of Wales, Heath Park, Cardiff, where an X-ray was done, and they said it was a sprain. I was sent home with a bandage and no follow-up. The pain did not go away. On 19th October 2026, my GP sent me for a repeat X-ray and MRI, which showed a displaced scaphoid waist fracture that has not healed. I now need surgery. I have missed class tests and weeks of shifts at my café job. I would like an explanation, an apology, changes to how A&E checks wrist injuries, and compensation for pain and lost earnings. I would also like to know how a case like this could be funded. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guideline D62 says: 'Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination.' Did the clinical examination at A&E sufficiently rule out a scaphoid fracture, and was MRI considered as first-line imaging as recommended? Please let me know if you can advise. You can reach me by email at elin.rhydderch@example.com or by phone on 07700 900582.
